title: Follow up and refine
summary: A so-so first answer is normal — say exactly what to change

steps.body:
The AI's first answer often isn't quite right. **That's normal** — no need to start over.

Just reply in the same chat and say exactly what to change:
- “The second paragraph is too long, cut it to 2 lines”
- “Add the price: 150 baht”
- “Make it sound friendlier”

If you only say **“Bad, rewrite it”**, the AI doesn't know what's wrong, so it just keeps guessing.

Tip: also say **which parts are good and should stay**.

steps.prompt:
First ask: Write a LINE message inviting regular customers to my café, because we opened a new branch
(The AI wrote 3 long, formal paragraphs with no promotion)

Follow-up: Good start, but change 3 things:
1. Keep it to 4 lines max
2. Add the deal: buy 1 get 1 free, Nov 1–3, at our Nimman branch
3. Make it casual, like texting a friend
The thank-you line at the end is great, keep it
steps.output:
Big news! Our new Nimman branch is open ☕
To celebrate: buy 1 get 1 free on every drink, Nov 1–3 only
Come say hi, we'd love to see you 😊
Thanks for always supporting us 🙏
steps.note: A good follow-up lists what to change, what to add and what to keep, so the AI gets it right in one go.

steps.question: The AI wrote a birthday message for your boss, but it's too long and too gushy. Which follow-up works best?
options: Cut it to 2 lines, use a polite workplace tone, and remove the word “dear”
steps.explain: Option 2 names the length, the tone and the word to remove, so the AI knows exactly what to fix. The others never say what the problem is.

steps.task:
You asked the AI for a Facebook post announcing new opening hours for your noodle shop. Its answer had these problems:
- Two big paragraphs, tiring to read
- Stiff, official tone, like a government notice
- It left out the new hours: 7:00–15:00, closed Wednesdays
- The thank-you to customers was good

Write **one follow-up message** that tells the AI exactly what to fix.
rubric: Gives a specific length (e.g. how many lines or sentences)
Asks to add the missing info: 7:00–15:00 and closed Wednesdays
Names the new tone wanted (e.g. friendly, warm)
Says to keep the good part (the thank-you) instead of a vague full rewrite
